intro: Bavaria’s capital: beer halls, baroque churches, the English Garden and the Alps on the horizon.
areas: Marienplatz, the Glockenspiel and the Viktualienmarkt.
University district beside the huge park.
sights: Huge park with surfers on the Eisbach.
night: Around Sendlinger Tor and the Kunstpark area.
arrive: Munich Airport is linked by S-Bahn (S1 and S8). Munich Hauptbahnhof has trains across Europe.
pass: MVV day tickets or the Deutschlandticket; check current fares.
when: May–September; Oktoberfest (book very early); December markets.
tip: Hotels triple in price during Oktoberfest; book months ahead.

intro: Germany’s port city of canals, warehouses, the Elbphilharmonie and the Reeperbahn.
areas: World Heritage warehouses and the Elbphilharmonie.
Alternative district of cafés and bars.
sights: Concert hall with a free public plaza.
eat: Bread rolls filled with herring or other fish.
arrive: Hamburg Airport is linked by S-Bahn (S1). Hamburg Hauptbahnhof has trains across Germany.
around: U-Bahn, S-Bahn, buses and HADAG ferries (part of public transport).
pass: HVV day tickets or the Deutschlandticket; check current fares.
tip: Ride ferry line 62 for a cheap harbour tour.

intro: A Rhineland city of a mighty cathedral, Kölsch beer and carnival.
sights: Modern art, including Pop Art and Picasso.
eat: Halve Hahn and Himmel un Ääd.
night: Clubs and music venues in a former industrial area.
arrive: Cologne Bonn Airport is linked by S-Bahn. Köln Hbf, next to the cathedral, has trains across Europe.
pass: KVB tickets or the Deutschlandticket; check current fares.
when: May–September; carnival in February; December markets.
tip: Your Kölsch glass will keep being refilled until you put a beer mat on top.

intro: ‘Mainhattan’: a skyline of towers beside a rebuilt old town, cider taverns and museums.
sights: Major art collection from the Middle Ages to today.
eat: Market hall with local food stalls.
night: Bars and clubs near the main station.
Concert hall in a restored opera house.
arrive: Frankfurt Airport has S-Bahn and long-distance train stations. Hauptbahnhof is the city hub.
pass: RMV tickets or the Deutschlandticket; check current fares.
tip: Trade fairs fill hotels; check the fair calendar before booking.

intro: The Netherlands’ architecture city: bold buildings, a giant port and a cool food scene.
sights: Food hall with a painted arch.
Tilted cube-shaped homes by Piet Blom.
eat: Food stalls under a giant painted arch.
Battered fish pieces, a Dutch street snack.
arrive: Rotterdam The Hague Airport is small; Schiphol is 25–30 minutes by train. Rotterdam Centraal has fast trains.
around: Metro, trams, buses and water taxis.
pass: RET day tickets or OVpay; check current fares.
tip: Take a water taxi across the Maas.

intro: A canal city with sunken wharves, a medieval cathedral tower and a young student vibe.
areas: Museum district with the Centraal Museum.
sights: Tallest church tower in the Netherlands.
De Stijl icon and World Heritage site.
arrive: Schiphol Airport is about 30 minutes by train. Utrecht Centraal is the Netherlands’ biggest rail hub.
around: Walk or cycle; buses and trams.
pass: OVpay contactless or day tickets; check current fares.
tip: Book the Dom Tower climb in advance.

intro: Europe’s capital: the Grand-Place, art nouveau, comics and great beer and chocolate.
areas: Guild houses and the Manneken Pis.
eat: Light Brussels waffles and dense Liège waffles.
night: Bars around the old market hall.
arrive: Brussels Airport is linked by train (about 20 minutes). Brussels-Midi has Eurostar and high-speed trains.
pass: STIB tickets, day passes or contactless; check current fares.
tip: Look for the Flower Carpet in mid-August of even years.

intro: Belgium’s fashion and diamond city, with Rubens, a grand station and a lively port.
eat: Antwerp’s own beer, served in a ‘bolleke’ glass.
night: Bars and restaurants around the museums.
Waterside bars in the old docks.
A big club scene, especially at weekends.
arrive: Brussels Airport is about 35 minutes by train. Antwerpen-Centraal has trains to Brussels and Amsterdam.
pass: De Lijn tickets; check current options.
tip: Climb to the MAS rooftop for free city views.

intro: A fairy-tale medieval town of canals, belfries and chocolate shops.
areas: The two main squares, with the Belfry and town hall.
sights: See the town from the water.
eat: Frites from stands on the Markt.
night: Historic bars with long Belgian beer lists.
arrive: Brussels Airport is about 90 minutes by train; Bruges station is a short walk from the centre.
pass: De Lijn buses; check current options.
tip: Stay overnight; the town empties after day-trippers leave.

intro: A medieval city with a student buzz: canals, a castle and the Ghent Altarpiece.
arrive: Brussels Airport is about an hour by train. Gent-Sint-Pieters station links to Brussels and Bruges.
around: Trams and buses; walking and cycling.
pass: De Lijn tickets; check current options.
when: April–September; July for the Ghent Festivities.

intro: Mozart’s birthplace, with a baroque old town, a hilltop fortress and The Sound of Music.
sights: Gardens from The Sound of Music.
arrive: Salzburg Airport is linked by bus. Salzburg Hbf has trains to Vienna and Munich.
pass: Salzburg Card covers transport and attractions; check current options.
when: May–September; July–August for the Festival; Advent markets.

intro: Switzerland’s largest city: a lake, an old town, art and Alpine views.
night: Clubs and bars in former factories.
arrive: Zurich Airport has trains to the main station (about 10–15 minutes).
pass: ZVV day tickets or the Zürich Card; check current fares.
tip: Swim in the river at a badi in summer.

intro: A lakeside city of diplomacy, watchmaking and Alpine views.
sights: Climb the towers for lake views.
night: Bars and cafés in an Italianate village.
Lake bathing and fondue in winter.
arrive: Geneva Airport has trains to Cornavin (about 7 minutes). Hotels give guests a free transport card.
pass: Geneva Transport Card from your hotel; check current conditions.
tip: Ask your hotel for the free Geneva Transport Card.
